explanation: Cabral did not sail to find Brazil and the treaty did not send him; what the treaty did was decide in advance what a landfall there would mean. Taking possession in the name of Manuel I was an act with a legal addressee — Castile — and it worked because the coast lay east of the meridian agreed six years earlier. The claim here is narrow and is the weakest of the five types on purpose: the line did not cause the voyage, it is what made the voyage a claim.
